why: No repository is present on this machine (repository.url is null, cloned=false) and the only code pointer in the contract is a Zenodo archive (10.5281/zenodo.21831681) that has not been fetched, so there is nothing to run. The match target (C1) is nonetheless a self-contained, fully specified numerical check: an additive chi-square-family statistic on the 3x3, N=18 margin fibre with 406 tables, compared against brute-force multiple-hypergeometric enumeration. The cell-separable DP (Wallenius/Fisher noncentral hypergeometric cell factorization with four moment accumulators) is described in enough algorithmic detail in the paper to reimplement, and the reference side is a 406-table enumeration, so no authors' artifacts are strictly required. If the Zenodo archive turns out to be reachable, this immediately upgrades to full_release (entrypoints exact_moments_dp.py / exact_moments_dp_fast.py).

compute.basis: C1 is a 406-table enumeration plus a 3x3 cell-by-cell DP with four accumulators (paper: 5.5 ms); the only real cost is reimplementing the DP and the reference enumerator, and the command-time budget covers a numpy/scipy install, the verification run, and a clean re-run well inside a few minutes on 8 CPU cores.
